claims.claim: Facebook's Like button was first enabled on February 9, 2009.
claims.episode_span: The Like button launched publicly on 9 February 2009
claims.supporting_quote: The like button on the social networking website Facebook was first enabled on February 9, 2009.

claims.claim: Rosenstein coded the prototype in an all-night session around 2007, when it was called the 'awesome' button.
claims.episode_span: Rosenstein later recalled that the group spent weeks debating the exact wording and icon, ultimately rejecting “Awesome” and “+1” in favor of the single word “Like”
claims.source_title: 'Our minds can be hijacked': the tech insiders who fear a smartphone dystopia | The Guardian
claims.supporting_quote: A decade after he stayed up all night coding a prototype of what was then called an “awesome” button

claims.claim: During development the feature was internally the 'awesome button'; engineers considered a star, plus/minus and heart designs before it was renamed at Mark Zuckerberg's direction.
claims.episode_span: the group spent weeks debating the exact wording and icon
claims.supporting_quote: During development, engineers, including Andrew Bosworth , Leah Pearlman and Justin Rosenstein, initially considered designs based on a star, a plus/minus button, or a heart, and the feature was internally referred to as the "awesome button" before being renamed at Mark Zuckerberg 's direction.

claims.claim: By 2017 Rosenstein had imposed strict limits on his own social-media use (blocking Reddit, banning himself from Snapchat, limiting Facebook).
claims.episode_span: By 2017 Rosenstein had left Facebook and begun limiting his own use of social media
claims.source_title: 'Our minds can be hijacked': the tech insiders who fear a smartphone dystopia | The Guardian
claims.supporting_quote: had tweaked his laptop’s operating system to block Reddit, banned himself from Snapchat, which he compares to heroin, and imposed limits on his use of Facebook

claims.claim: In May 2019 Instagram began tests hiding the number of likes on posts from other users.
claims.episode_span: Instagram ran experiments in 2019 that hid Like counts from other users in several countries
claims.supporting_quote: In May 2019, Instagram began tests wherein the number of likes on a user's post is hidden from other users.

claims.claim: YouTube switched from star ratings to Like/Dislike buttons in early 2010.
claims.episode_span: Twitter introduced Favorites the same year, YouTube added thumbs-up ratings, and Instagram launched with a heart icon in 2010
claims.supporting_quote: In early 2010, as part of a broader redesign of the service, YouTube switched from a star-based rating system to Like/Dislike buttons.
